simple.meaning: פְּאֵר (pᵉʼêr) is a Hebrew word meaning “an embellishment , i.e. fancy head-dress.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פְּאֵר (H6287) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 39:28, with occurrences in Exodus, Isaiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּאֵר (H6287) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פְּאֵר (H6287) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פְּאֵר (pᵉʼêr) / H6287 is traced through Exodus 39:28, Isaiah 3:20, Isaiah 61:3, Isaiah 61:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6287. p 'er מְּאֵר noun masculine Ezek 44:18 head-dress, turban (? originally ornament ); — absolute ׳פ of bridegroom Isa 61:10 , sign of joy 61:3 (opposed to mourning, and so) מְּאֵרְךָ Ezek 24:17 , plural suffix מְּאֵרֵכֶם 24:23 (worn by men of position); of priests פִשְׁתִּים מַּאֲרֵי 44:18 , שֵׁשׁמּ ׳הַמִּנְבָּעֹת Exod 39:28 (P); plural absolute מְּאֵרִים Isa 3:20 (of luxurious women).

occurrences.englishText: the turban of fine linen, the linen headbands of fine linen, the linen trousers of fine twined linen,
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume containers, the charms,
to provide for those who mourn in Zion,
I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!
Sigh, but not aloud. Make no mourning for the dead. Bind your headdress on you, and put your sandals on your feet. Don’t cover your lips, and don’t eat mourner’s bread.”
Your turbans will be on your heads, and your sandals on your feet. You won’t mourn or weep; but you will pine away in your iniquities, and moan one toward another.
They shall have linen turbans on their heads, and shall have linen trousers on their waists. They shall not clothe themselves with anything that makes them sweat.
